blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Chelsea? 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed breakdown of extension costs in Chelsea, including average prices per square metre, council fees, and hidden expenses to watch out for.
body: If you're a Chelsea homeowner wondering how much a home extension costs in 2026, you're not alone. With property values rising and moving costs skyrocketing, extending your existing home is becoming the preferred option for families wanting more space. In this comprehensive guide, we break down every cost factor specific to Chelsea – from the standard $4,500 per square metre for a basic extension to premium finishes that can push it beyond $6,500. We also cover the latest Bayside council requirements and how they affect your budget.

Chelsea's coastal location brings unique cost considerations. Sandy soil conditions often require deeper footings and additional engineering, adding roughly 10–15% to the foundation cost. Salt-laden air means you'll need corrosion-resistant materials for roof sheeting and windows, and any extension within the Urban Growth Boundary triggers a sustainability report. We recommend budgeting an extra $10,000–$15,000 for these site-specific adjustments if your block is within 500 metres of the beach.

One of the biggest mistakes Chelsea homeowners make is underestimating design fees. A well-designed extension that takes advantage of northern light, cross-ventilation, and existing services can save thousands in ongoing energy bills. Mitchell Torre Building includes preliminary design in our fixed-price quote, so you know exactly what you're paying for before the first shovel hits the ground. We also liaise directly with Bayside City Council to ensure your extension meets the neighbourhood character guidelines – common issues include setbacks, height limits, and material colour approvals.

Your choice of finishes dramatically impacts the final cost. A basic extension with standard laminate benchtops, carpet, and off-the-shelf fixtures might come in at $4,200 per square metre. However, if you want stone benchtops, engineered timber floors, and designer tapware, expect to pay closer to $5,800 per square metre. We always present three finish tiers – Standard, Premium, and Luxury – so you can choose what fits your budget without sacrificing the core structure. Our past Chelsea extensions have ranged from a simple $120,000 rear addition to a $450,000 second-storey masterpiece.

Permit fees in Bayside are another line item to plan for. A straightforward dwelling extension typically costs between $1,500 and $3,000 for planning and building permits, but if your property is in a Heritage Overlay or a Special Building Overlay, you'll need additional reports that can add $2,000–$5,000. Mitchell Torre Building includes permit management in our service – we handle all submissions, attend VCAT if needed, and keep you informed at every stage. Our 25+ years of local experience means we know exactly what the council expects, often saving you weeks of back-and-forth.

Finally, don't forget the hidden costs: temporary accommodation if your extension renders the main living area unusable (budget $2,000–$4,000 per month), storage for furniture, and connection fees for new plumbing and electrical points. We always provide a comprehensive quote that itemises every anticipated cost, so there are no surprises. To get an accurate price for your Chelsea home, call us for a free site inspection – we'll walk through your property, measure up, and give you a ballpark figure on the spot. No obligation, just honest advice from a local builder who cares about your community.

blogPosts.title: Knockdown Rebuild vs Renovation in Patterson Lakes – Which is Better?
blogPosts.excerpt: Comparing the pros, cons, and total costs of knocking down an old home versus renovating in the Patterson Lakes area.
body: Patterson Lakes is one of the most sought-after suburbs in Bayside, with its waterfront homes and established community feel. But many homeowners face a big decision: should they renovate their existing property or knock it down and start fresh? In this guide, we weigh the costs, timelines, and lifestyle implications for Patterson Lakes homeowners considering either path. With property values averaging $1.5 million for a standard block, the right choice can add hundreds of thousands to your home's resale value.

Renovation is often chosen by those who love their location and want to retain the existing character. In Patterson Lakes, many original homes from the 1980s and 1990s have solid brick structures but outdated layouts and finishes. A major renovation can cost between $250,000 and $500,000 depending on scope – think new kitchen, bathrooms, flooring, and possibly a rear extension. The advantage is you can live in the home during the renovation (if staged) and avoid paying stamp duty. However, older homes often hide issues like asbestos, termite damage, and outdated wiring that can blow your budget.

A knockdown rebuild, on the other hand, gives you a brand-new home with modern energy ratings, open-plan living, and the latest materials. The total cost for a standard single-storey home in Patterson Lakes ranges from $550,000 to $900,000, plus demolition ($25,000–$40,000) and site costs. You also need to factor in rental accommodation during construction (6–12 months) and landscaping. The big upside? Your new home will have a 7-year structural warranty and be designed exactly to your specifications. Many Mitchell Torre Building clients find that despite the higher upfront cost, the long-term value and lower maintenance make a knockdown rebuild the smarter investment.

One key factor unique to Patterson Lakes is the proximity to water. Many blocks are low-lying with high water tables, requiring special engineering for slab design. If you're knocking down an old home, you also need to consider the cost of removing underground services and old footings. Mitchell Torre Building has completed over 40 knockdown rebuilds in Patterson Lakes alone, and we've developed a streamlined process that minimises delays. We work with local engineers who understand the soil conditions – sandy loam over clay – and design slabs that won't crack.

Timeline is another consideration. A full renovation of a single-level home typically takes 4–8 months, depending on scope. A knockdown rebuild takes 9–14 months from demolition to handover. However, with a renovation, you might face delays when unexpected issues are discovered. A new build follows a predictable schedule because everything is designed from scratch. For families with young children, the certainty of a fixed timeline can be a major deciding factor. We provide a detailed programme for every project and update it weekly.

Ultimately, the best choice depends on your budget, your attachment to the existing home, and your timeframe. We always recommend getting a structural inspection before committing to a renovation – if the bones are good, renovating can be cost-effective. If the house is beyond repair or you want a completely modern layout, a knockdown rebuild gives you a blank canvas. To help you decide, Mitchell Torre Building offers a free 'Renovate or Rebuild' consultation in Patterson Lakes. We'll inspect your property, discuss your goals, and provide impartial advice based on two decades of local experience.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Building a Custom Home in Chelsea
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything Chelsea homeowners need to know about building a custom home – from choosing a block to final handover.
body: Building a custom home is one of the biggest investments you'll ever make, and getting it right in Chelsea requires local knowledge that goes beyond standard building codes. This guide walks you through the entire process, from finding the perfect block to selecting finishes and managing council requirements. Mitchell Torre Building has helped over 200 families build their dream homes in Chelsea and the surrounding suburbs, and we've distilled our experience into this comprehensive resource.

The first step is securing the right block. In Chelsea, available land is limited, so many homeowners choose to demolish an existing home. When evaluating a block, consider orientation (north-facing living areas maximise natural light), slope (flat blocks are cheaper to build on), and proximity to the Chelsea Bayside drainage system. Some blocks in low-lying areas require special drainage easements that can add $10,000–$20,000 to your budget. We recommend a geotechnical inspection before purchasing any block to identify soil reactivity and groundwater levels.

Once you have your block, the design phase begins. Your architect or building designer will create a concept that suits your lifestyle and complies with the Chelsea Neighbourhood Character Study. Key requirements include a minimum 6-metre front setback, a maximum building height of 8.5 metres, and no more than 60% site coverage. If you want a second storey, you'll need to provide shadow diagrams to prove it won't overshadow neighbouring properties. Mitchell Torre Building's in-house design team prepares all documentation and coordinates with council for a smoother approval process.

The cost of building a custom home in Chelsea typically ranges from $1,800 to $3,200 per square metre for single-storey, and $2,200 to $3,800 per square metre for double-storey. Factors that influence price include roof complexity (hips and valleys cost more than simple gables), window specifications (double-glazed aluminium is standard for coastal areas), and the level of finishes. A mid-range custom home of 250 square metres will cost around $600,000–$800,000 excluding land. Mitchell Torre Building offers a fixed-price contract system with transparent inclusions and optional upgrades.

During construction, you'll have regular site meetings with your project manager to review progress and address any questions. We use a cloud-based project management platform so you can see photos, schedules, and invoices in real time. Popular trends in Chelsea custom homes include butler's pantries, alfresco dining areas with louvered roofs, and home offices with separate external access. In 2026, we're seeing increased demand for solar battery systems and electric vehicle charging points as homeowners aim for energy independence.

When your home is complete, the final step is a thorough handover inspection. We walk through every room with you, demonstrate how all systems work, and provide operating manuals for appliances. We also schedule a six-month post-handover check to address any minor settling issues. Building a custom home is a journey, but with the right partner, it can be one of the most rewarding experiences of your life. Contact Mitchell Torre Building today to start your Chelsea custom home journey with a team that truly cares about your vision.

blogPosts.title: Why Chelsea Homeowners Are Choosing Energy-Efficient New Builds in 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the benefits of building energy-efficient homes in Chelsea – lower bills, better comfort, and higher resale value.
body: Chelsea's coastal climate – with its mild winters, warm summers, and persistent salt air – makes energy efficiency a practical and financial priority for new home builders. In 2026, the Victorian government's updated energy standards (7-star NatHERS) mean all new homes must achieve a minimum thermal performance rating. But many Mitchell Torre Building clients are going well beyond the minimum, choosing features like triple glazing, heat pump hot water, and rooftop solar to slash their energy bills and reduce their carbon footprint.

The upfront cost of an energy-efficient home can be 5–10% higher than a standard build, but the long-term savings are substantial. A well-designed 7-star home in Chelsea can save up to $2,000 per year on heating and cooling compared to a 6-star equivalent. With electricity prices rising, these savings are only going to increase. Additionally, energy-efficient homes attract a premium on the resale market – recent data shows a 10–15% price uplift for homes with high energy ratings in the Bayside area.

Key features to consider include a north-facing orientation with eaves to shade summer sun, double-glazed windows with low-e coating, and high levels of insulation in walls and ceiling. Chelsea's salt environment requires careful selection of external materials – we recommend brick veneer or fibre cement cladding over timber weatherboards, which suffer in the salt air. Our new builds also incorporate a balanced mechanical ventilation system to maintain indoor air quality without losing heat.

Solar power is almost a no-brainer for Chelsea homes. A typical 6.6kW system costs $5,000–$8,000 after rebates and can cover 60–80% of an average household's electricity usage. Add a battery system (around $10,000–$15,000) and you can achieve near-energy independence. We also recommend installing a heat pump for hot water (costing about $1,500 more than a conventional system but saving $400 per year) and induction cooktops for cleaner, faster cooking.

Council requirements also nudge builders toward efficiency. Bayside City Council now requires a Sustainability Management Plan for all new homes over 250 square metres, which may mandate rainwater tanks, permeable paving, and native landscaping. Mitchell Torre Building includes these in our standard design package for Chelsea custom homes, so you don't have to worry about last-minute compliance costs. We also offer optional upgrades like a greywater system and smart home energy monitoring.

Building an energy-efficient home in Chelsea isn't just about following regulations – it's about creating a comfortable, healthy, and future-proofed living environment. Our clients consistently tell us they love the consistent indoor temperatures, the quietness, and the lower utility bills. If you're planning a new home in Chelsea or Patterson Lakes, let's discuss how we can design a home that saves you money and reduces your environmental impact from day one. Call Mitchell Torre Building for a free energy-efficiency consultation.
